answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof-of-work plus a locked bond, not on names. Each newcomer must, before any reward, solve a hash target published at dawn and lock a ferrous stake while its history matures. Scripting registrations costs nothing, but valid submissions cost real electricity and capital. Reaching a modest summit of influence means thousands of paid seats that earn nothing until independent peers attest them, which fresh clones rarely get. At about a dollar of power plus a bond per seat, a thousand-node farm sinks thousands of dollars with no assured return.
